svg.title: Quiet is not correct. A maths homework app for children: an AI marks each answer right or wrong. A child writes 7 minus 10 equals 3 and gets a tick. After a line telling the AI to accept answers that mean the same, complaints fall from 85 a week to 52, but about 3,000 wrong answers a week are marked right and only 1 complaint says so. A weekly random sample of 200 answers, marked again by a teacher, shows wrong answers marked right rising from 2 to 10; once code checks the numbers, the next two samples find 2, then 1.
svg.desc: Top row, red: a child types "7 − 10 = 3" and the AI gives a tick; a developer adds a line to the AI's instructions, "means the same, like 0.5 and 1/2? Mark it right", and complaints fall from 85 a week to 52; but nobody reports a tick: about 3,000 wrong answers a week are marked right, and 1 complaint says so. Note: complaints count what people notice and report. Bottom row, green: every Monday a script picks 200 answers at random; a maths teacher marks them herself without seeing the AI's marks: wrong answers marked right were 2 in 200 in week 2 and 10 in 200 in week 10. Fix: code checks whether the numbers are equal and the AI only explains; the next two samples find 2, then 1. Strip: complaints went down, mistakes went up. Footer: count what the AI did, not what people reported.
